passage.quote:
A parallel backward implementation uses the actual stored forward weights and
incoming sensitivities to compute a dot product, differences and input gradients.
Its execution, storage and numerical bounds connect to TorchLean’s true
real-valued derivative, with inherited forward error kept explicit.

summary: Compute the softmax vector-Jacobian product with an explicit parallel dot product, difference pass and multiplication pass on actual stored operands.
Derive finite intermediate values and gradient error from bounded original inputs, preserving forward approximation and arithmetic rounding errors.
Prove universal admitted-run correctness, independent execution existence and memory safety with explicit storage and phase interfaces.

from.quote:
The backward takes the actual stored softmax outputs and a row of incoming
sensitivities: numbers describing how strongly each output contributes to a
surrounding result. For ideal weights p and sensitivities g, it returns
p_i*(g_i-q), where q is the sum of p_j*g_j over the row. This is the true
vector-Jacobian product of the ideal real-valued softmax. The supplied PTX
program is developed separately from TorchLean's automatic backward construction.
It does not differentiate floating-point rounding or the approximate exponential.

passage.quote:
theorem rowBackward_is_vjp (values incoming : Vec n) (positive : 0<n) (i : Fin n) :
    rowBackward values.ofLp incoming.ofLp i =
      (VJP[fun v : Vec n => getScalarE
        (Activation.softmaxSpec (α:=ℝ) (s:=[n]) 0 (ofFnE v)), values] incoming).ofLp i

from.quote:
The implementation first computes qHat, an approximation of q, by combining
pairwise sums in a balanced tree. It reuses the existing parallel reduction
with one row, stored forward outputs as inputs, sensitivities as weights, and
positive-zero bias. Multiplication at each leaf and addition at
each tree node remain actual rounded instructions. A parallel difference pass
loads each sensitivity and the stored qHat, multiplies qHat by exact minus one, and
adds that result to the sensitivity. A parallel multiplication pass then loads
each stored forward output and difference and writes the gradient. The separate
passes favor reuse of checked execution and memory contracts; fusion is outside
this component. Multiplying by minus one and adding does not claim a new
subtraction-instruction formalization.

passage.quote:
def body : Op → List Instr
  | .copy => [localOp (.mov32 6 (.reg 5))]
  | .mul => [.binary32 ⟨.always,.mul,6,.reg 4,.reg 5⟩]
  | .gate => [localOp (.mov32 6 (.reg 5)),localOp (.setp .eq 1 (.reg 4) (.imm 0)),clear,
      localOp (.setp .ge 1 (.reg 4) (.imm 0x80000000)),clear]
  | .difference => [.binary32 ⟨.always,.mul,6,.reg 5,.imm 0xbf800000⟩,
      .binary32 ⟨.always,.add,6,.reg 4,.reg 6⟩]

inductive Run (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d) (p g : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) : List Word → Prop
  | phases {dot differences final : List Word}
      (dotRun : SoftmaxBackwardDot.Launch d p g dot)
      (differenceRun : Pointwise.Launch .difference (differenceLayout d bound) (extend d dot) differences)
      (gradientRun : Pointwise.Launch .mul (gradientLayout d bound) (extend d differences) final) :
      Run d bound p g final

from.quote:
The forward output prefix is retained as storage when forward scratch is
released. Incoming sensitivities and fresh scratch are supplied in separately
specified regions of the resulting memory buffer, called the arena. These allocation and storage-view
operations perform no derivative arithmetic. Original row inputs and values passed
between launches come from fetched loads; arithmetic intermediates come from
actual instructions. Each dot product and difference passed to the next phase
comes from an actual store. Sources remain read-only during each pointwise pass, and
each output cell has one writer. Entry pointers are an explicit input interface,
not a CUDA argument-passing proof. Completed phase boundaries retain the existing
model-level waiting and initialization contract.

passage.quote:
inductive FullRun (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d)
    (input incoming : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) : List Word → Prop
  | phases {forward final : List Word}
      (forwardRun : Scalar.SoftmaxParallel.Run d input forward)
      (backwardRun : Run d bound (SoftmaxStorage.row (Sum.width d) forward) incoming final) :
      FullRun d bound input incoming final

theorem entry_is_storage_view (run : Scalar.SoftmaxParallel.Run d input forward)
    (incoming : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) :
    SoftmaxBackwardDot.global d (SoftmaxStorage.row (Sum.width d) forward) incoming =
      forward.take (Sum.width d) ++ List.ofFn incoming ++ [0,0]

from.quote:
For n entries, words 0 through n-1 retain the forward outputs and words n
through 2*n-1 hold incoming sensitivities. Word 2*n is the positive-zero bias,
and word 2*n+1 holds the computed dot product. The difference pass appends n
output words starting at 2*n+2; the multiplication pass appends n gradient words
starting at 3*n+2. The final arena has 4*n+2 words and preserves both input rows.

passage.quote:
def differenceLayout (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d) : Pointwise.Layout (Sum.width d) where
  prefixWords := differenceBase d
  left := fun i => Sum.width d+i.val
  right := fun _ => Sum.outputIndex d
  leftBound := by intro i; have := i.isLt; unfold differenceBase; omega
  rightBound := by intro i; unfold differenceBase Sum.outputIndex; omega
  small := by have := width_bound d bound; unfold differenceBase; omega

passage.quote:
def gradientLayout (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d) : Pointwise.Layout (Sum.width d) where
  prefixWords := gradientBase d
  left := fun i => i.val
  right := fun i => differenceBase d+i.val
  leftBound := by intro i; have := i.isLt; unfold gradientBase; omega
  rightBound := by intro i; have := i.isLt; unfold differenceBase gradientBase; omega
  small := by have := width_bound d bound; unfold gradientBase; omega

from.quote:
The first domain retains nonempty power-of-two rows of at most 1024 entries.
For accuracy, original scores are finite, have magnitude at most 2^124, and
satisfy the forward guard: the accumulated exponential and sum error allowance
is at most one half.
Incoming encoded sensitivities are finite and have magnitude at most 2^60.
Their exact real values are the initial backward reference inputs. Forward
accuracy and the numerical normalization proof bound the actual stored weights;
the derived weight magnitude is at most four. Products, the dot result,
differences and gradients have respective magnitude bounds 2^62, 2^72, 2^73
and 2^75, establishing finite encoded results. These conservative bounds leave
room for signed accumulation without requiring intermediate range premises. Successful intermediate execution, intermediate
finiteness and final gradient accuracy are conclusions rather than caller premises.
The gradient error includes the inherited forward error, rounded dot-product
error, difference error and final multiplication error, each kept explicit.

passage.quote:
theorem forward_report (d : Nat) (bound : d≤10)
    (input : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (values : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ)
    (finite : ∀i, finiteReal (input i)=some (values i))
    (small : ∀i, |values i|≤(2:ℝ)^(124:ℤ))
    (guard : SoftmaxPipeline.AccuracyGuard d values)
    (run : Scalar.SoftmaxParallel.Run d input forward) :
    ∃ (m : ℝ) (u : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ),
      finiteReal (Scalar.SoftmaxPipeline.maximumWord d input)=some m ∧
      ∀i, finiteReal forward[i.val]! =some (resultValue d u i) ∧
        |resultValue d u i|≤4 ∧
        |resultValue d u i-Softmax.rowForward values i|≤coordinateAllowance d values m u i

theorem accuracy (g p : Nat → Word) (gv pv : Nat → ℝ) (k offset : Nat) (out : Word)
    (depth : k≤10)
    (finiteG : ∀j, j<2^k → finiteReal (g (offset+j))=some (gv (offset+j)))
    (finiteP : ∀j, j<2^k → finiteReal (p (offset+j))=some (pv (offset+j)))
    (smallG : ∀j, j<2^k → |gv (offset+j)|≤(2:ℝ)^60)
    (smallP : ∀j, j<2^k → |pv (offset+j)|≤4)
    (allowed : Reduction.Eval (Reduction.balanced k offset (fun j => (g j,p j))) out) :
    finiteReal out=some (rounded gv pv k offset) ∧
    |rounded gv pv k offset|≤(2:ℝ)^(k+62) ∧
    |rounded gv pv k offset-ideal gv pv k offset|≤budget gv pv k offset

theorem output_accuracy (d : Nat) (bound : Sum.Bounds d)
    (p g : Fin (Sum.width d) → Word) (pv gv : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ) (out : Word)
    (finiteP : ∀i,finiteReal (p i)=some (pv i))
    (finiteG : ∀i,finiteReal (g i)=some (gv i))
    (smallP : ∀i,|pv i|≤4) (smallG : ∀i,|gv i|≤(2:ℝ)^60)
    (allowed : Output d p g out) :
    finiteReal out=some (BackwardDot.vector_rounded d gv pv) ∧
    |BackwardDot.vector_rounded d gv pv|≤(2:ℝ)^72 ∧
    |BackwardDot.vector_rounded d gv pv-∑i,pv i*gv i|≤BackwardDot.vector_budget d gv pv

passage.quote:
theorem stages (p g dot negative diff out : Word) (pv gv q : ℝ)
    (pFinite : finiteReal p=some pv) (gFinite : finiteReal g=some gv)
    (dotFinite : finiteReal dot=some q)
    (pSmall : |pv|≤4) (gSmall : |gv|≤(2:ℝ)^60) (qSmall : |q|≤(2:ℝ)^72)
    (negate : Results .mul dot 0xbf800000 negative)
    (subtract : Results .add g negative diff) (multiply : Results .mul p diff out) :
    finiteReal negative=some (-q) ∧ finiteReal diff=some (difference gv q) ∧
    finiteReal out=some (gradient pv gv q) ∧
    |difference gv q|≤(2:ℝ)^73 ∧ |gradient pv gv q|≤(2:ℝ)^75 ∧
    |difference gv q-(gv-q)|≤subError gv q ∧
    |gradient pv gv q-pv*difference gv q|≤mulError pv gv q

from.quote:
Write epsilon_i for the inherited error of stored pHat_i from ideal p_i.
The dot rounding allowance sigmaDot sums half-grid-spacing errors at every
leaf product and tree addition on their actual rounded operands. With
q=sum_j p_j*g_j, Q=sigmaDot+sum_j abs(g_j)*epsilon_j bounds the dot error.
The stored gradient error is at most
`mulError_i + abs(g_i-q)*epsilon_i + abs(pHat_i)*(subError_i+Q)`.
Here subError_i bounds rounding of g_i-qHat, and mulError_i bounds rounding of
pHat_i times that rounded difference. Multiplication of the finite qHat by
minus one is exact as a real value. Incoming values have no additional
quantization allowance because the reference uses their exact stored values.

passage.quote:
def budget (g p : Nat → ℝ) : Nat → Nat → ℝ
  | 0,offset => eps32 (g offset*p offset)
  | k+1,offset => eps32 (rounded g p k offset+rounded g p k (offset+2^k))+
    budget g p k offset+budget g p k (offset+2^k)

theorem output_accuracy (d : Nat) (bound : d≤10)
    (g p : Fin (2^d) → Word) (gv pv : Fin (2^d) → ℝ) (dot out : Word)
    (finiteG : ∀i,finiteReal (g i)=some (gv i))
    (finiteP : ∀i,finiteReal (p i)=some (pv i))
    (smallG : ∀i,|gv i|≤(2:ℝ)^60) (smallP : ∀i,|pv i|≤4)
    (tree : Reduction.Eval (Reduction.balanced d 0
      (fun j => ((List.ofFn g)[j]!, (List.ofFn p)[j]!))) dot)
    (zero : Results .add dot 0 out) :
    finiteReal out=some (vector_rounded d gv pv) ∧
    |vector_rounded d gv pv|≤(2:ℝ)^72 ∧
    |vector_rounded d gv pv-∑i,pv i*gv i|≤vector_budget d gv pv

def allowance (d : Nat) (ideal pv gv epsilon : Fin (Sum.width d) → ℝ) (i : Fin (Sum.width d)) : ℝ :=
  backwardBudget pv gv ideal epsilon (fun _=>0)
    (fun j=>SoftmaxBackwardNumeric.subError (gv j) (BackwardDot.vector_rounded d gv pv))
    (fun j=>SoftmaxBackwardNumeric.mulError (pv j) (gv j) (BackwardDot.vector_rounded d gv pv))
    (BackwardDot.vector_budget d gv pv) i

from.quote:
Every completed admitted backward execution satisfies the stored-output
contract and preserves its input regions. Separately, a finite schedule and its
memory-admission proof establish that a complete execution exists. Backward
alone has a witness for arbitrary input words; whole forward/backward existence
requires only the original finite-score domain, without an accuracy guard or
incoming finiteness. The stronger conditions above are needed for the numerical
comparison. All actual
accesses are checked for allocation bounds and alignment. The combined theorem
starts with original scores and incoming sensitivity words, runs forward and
backward, and compares the stored gradients with TorchLean's real derivative.
All results permitted by the arithmetic relations remain covered. Bitwise
agreement with a concrete PyTorch backend, arbitrary row lengths, masking,
fused execution, GPU progress and benchmarking remain separate obligations.

passage.quote:
theorem correct (run : Run d bound p g final) :
    final.length=4*Sum.width d+2 ∧
    (∀i : Fin (Sum.width d), final[i.val]?=some (p i) ∧
      final[Sum.width d+i.val]?=some (g i)) ∧
    ∃q, SoftmaxBackwardDot.Output d p g q ∧
      final[Sum.outputIndex d]?=some q ∧
      ∀i : Fin (Sum.width d), ∃negative difference,
        Results .mul q 0xbf800000 negative ∧
        Results .add (g i) negative difference ∧
        final[differenceBase d+i.val]?=some difference ∧
        Results .mul (p i) difference final[gradientBase d+i.val]!

passage.quote:
theorem access_safe (run : Run d bound p g final) :
    ∃dot differences, SoftmaxBackwardDot.Launch d p g dot ∧
      (∃denseBound : Dense.Bounds (Sum.shape d), ∃seeds,
        TraceSafe (Dense.config (Sum.shape d) denseBound) (Sum.program d)
          (Dense.initial (Sum.shape d) (SoftmaxBackwardDot.global d p g)
            (List.replicate (Sum.sharedWords d) 0) seeds) dot) ∧
      Pointwise.Launch .difference (differenceLayout d bound) (extend d dot) differences ∧
      PointwiseSafe .difference (differenceLayout d bound) (extend d dot) differences ∧
      Pointwise.Launch .mul (gradientLayout d bound) (extend d differences) final ∧
      PointwiseSafe .mul (gradientLayout d bound) (extend d differences) final

passage.quote:
The numerical theorem uses the exact real values of the original stored scores.
It derives the finite attained maximum, exponential range and approximation
errors, and the sum's rounding error. If the sum of exponential error allowances
plus (n-1)/8192 is at most one half, the computed denominator is at least one
half. Rounded reciprocal and product then remain finite. Each output is bounded
against the stable real softmax, retaining exponential, sum, reciprocal and
